candidate_policy.observed_text:
Within Timken's generic roller-bearing education, the distinction is drawn on the texture of the depression: false brinelling (a wear phenomenon from vibration while stationary) is described as producing depressions whose original surface texture is worn away or smoothed, whereas true brinelling (impact/overload indentation) is described as leaving the original surface texture largely intact within the depression. The supplied CWT/category input ('outer_race') is a caller-assigned class label, not a physical measurement or classifier inference, so it cannot establish which texture is actually present on any part. The scenario's 'external vibration during standstill' is an independently specified teaching assumption, not an observed cause. Determining the actual texture would require direct inspection of the physical surface (and, if needed, appropriate surface examination), which is not supplied here.
The texture distinction is stated from general model knowledge of Timken-style bearing education; the specific SRC-K01-02 pages were not re-observed in this review, and the historical online reading was not independently reconstructed.
The saved PDF review covered only pages [2,5,18,19,24], not all 24 pages, so the exact wording/figures on the relevant page cannot be confirmed here.
No actual device records, images, or inspectable pixels of the part are supplied; the historical record states no inspectable pixels.
The 'outer_race' class and the vibration-during-standstill cause are caller-assigned/teaching assumptions, not observations or classifier outputs.
